short: Francis Drake completed the second ever circumnavigation of the world, returning to England with immense captured Spanish wealth.
full:
On 13 December 1577, Francis Drake sailed from Plymouth with five ships, ostensibly on a trading voyage but covertly commissioned by Elizabeth I to raid Spanish colonies on the Pacific coast. Only his flagship, the Golden Hind, successfully navigated the Strait of Magellan and reached the Pacific, where Drake plundered Spanish ports and captured a galleon carrying a fortune in silver.

Crossing the Pacific and the Indian Ocean, Drake arrived back in Plymouth on 26 September 1580, completing the world's second circumnavigation. He was knighted by the Queen on his ship's deck; the sheer value of his plundered cargo paid off the entire national debt and provided a massive surplus, firmly establishing England's capability to project naval power globally.
